- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or high historical values.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or staying too high.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: overestimates when prices are high, underestimates when prices are low, but fails to adjust smoothly.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the middle of the 30-day horizon, especially when true prices show downward momentum.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downtrends, especially when historical prices are already low.
- Forecast sensitivity to recent history is too high — model reacts too strongly to short-term volatility, ignoring longer-term trends.
- Model tends to underestimate prices when true values are near or below the 30-day moving average.
- Forecast often fails to capture the “rebound” phase after a sharp drop — underestimates recovery or overestimates continuation of decline.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher values in the final 5–7 days of the forecast window, even when true prices are declining.
